Package neqsim.process.chemistry.scale

Class ValveScaleDrift

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.chemistry.scale.ValveScaleDrift
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ValveScaleDrift extends Object implements Serializable
Couples scale/solids deposition kinetics to the effective flow coefficient of a ThrottlingValve, so that gradual trim plugging can be simulated as a measurable drift in valve opening.

A valve that fouls does not fail suddenly: a deposit layer grows on the trim, the open flow area shrinks, the effective flow coefficient Kv drops, and the level/pressure controller opens the valve further to hold its setpoint. The observable signature is therefore a slow upward drift of the valve opening until it pins at 100% and control is lost. This class turns a deposit growth rate (mm/yr) into the foulingFraction consumed by ThrottlingValve.setFoulingFraction(double), and predicts the drift.

Deposition model: a uniform radial deposit of thickness t on a circular trim port of diameter d0 reduces the open flow area to A(t)/A0 = ((d0 - 2t)/d0)^2 for t < d0/2. Because a control valve's flow coefficient is proportional to its discharge area, the area-loss fraction is used directly as the valve fouling fraction: foulingFraction = 1 - A(t)/A0.

The deposit growth rate can be supplied directly with setGrowthRateMmPerYear(double) or taken from a ScaleKinetics result via setKinetics(ScaleKinetics) (its effective, rate-controlling growth rate is used). This is a screening-level integrity model (NACE TM0374, NORSOK M-001 informational) intended for relative ranking and time-to-plug estimation, not an absolute mass-balance prediction.

Typical usage inside a transient study: 


 ValveScaleDrift drift = new ValveScaleDrift(levelValve);
 drift.setPortDiameter(0.05); // 50 mm trim port
 drift.setKinetics(scaleKinetics); // effective growth rate from ScaleKinetics
 for (int day = 0; day < 60; day++) {
   drift.advance(1.0); // grow deposit one day, update valve foulingFraction
   process.run(); // controller compensates → opening drifts up
 }
 double daysToPin = drift.predictTimeToPinDays(cleanOpeningPercent);

    • predictOpeningPercent

      public double predictOpeningPercent(double cleanOpeningPercent)
      Predicts the valve opening required to pass the same flow as a clean valve at a given opening, using a linear-characteristic approximation. As the deposit grows, the opening required to hold the setpoint increases as cleanOpeningPercent / (1 - foulingFraction), capped at 100%.
      Parameters:
      cleanOpeningPercent - the opening [%] the clean valve held to pass the required flow
      Returns:
      the fouled-valve opening [%] required to hold the same flow, capped at 100

    • predictTimeToPinDays

      public double predictTimeToPinDays(double cleanOpeningPercent)
      Predicts the time for the valve opening to drift up to 100% (loss of controllability) for a valve holding a given clean-valve opening, using a linear-characteristic approximation.

      The opening pins at 100% once the open-area fraction falls below cleanOpeningPercent / 100. For a uniform radial deposit this happens at deposit thickness t_pin = (d0/2) * (1 - sqrt(cleanOpeningPercent/100)).

      Parameters:
      cleanOpeningPercent - the opening [%] the clean valve held to pass the required flow (0 < value ≤ 100)
      Returns:
      time until the opening reaches 100% [days], or positive infinity if it never pins (zero growth rate, unset diameter, or a clean opening already at/above 100%)
